title: One-dimensional formal laws and the formal inverse
notes: Over a commutative ring \(A\) with \(1\), the notes write \(F(x,y)=x+y+\sum_{i+k\ge2}a_{ik}x^iy^k\), require associativity, and obtain an inverse from the formal implicit-function argument.
statement: An associative one-dimensional formal law over \(A\) is a series \(F\in A[[x,y]]\) with \(F(x,0)=x\), \(F(0,y)=y\), and \(F(F(x,y),z)=F(x,F(y,z))\). There is a unique \(\iota(x)\in xA[[x]]\) satisfying \(F(x,\iota(x))=F(\iota(x),x)=0\); recursively \(\iota(x)=-x+O(x^2)\). Commutativity is an additional issue, recorded separately.
reconstruction: The unit identities are made explicit; they also follow from associativity and the displayed linear term. The term ``implicit-function theorem'' is formal coefficient recursion, requiring no analytic convergence.
fate: Classical definition and inverse construction: \citet[\S I]{lazard1955formal}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: an established algebraic definition.

title: Associativity does not force commutativity over every ring
notes: The parenthesis reads \ru{коммутативность (она сл. из ассоц.)}: commutativity follows from associativity.
statement: The unrestricted assertion is false. It is true over a reduced coefficient ring, and also over a torsion-free coefficient ring. Over \(\mathbb F_p[a]/(a^2)\), \(F(x,y)=x+y+axy^p\) is associative and not commutative; the notebook itself supplies this counterexample in 1972-285.6.
reconstruction: The extra hypotheses are editorial repairs, not present in this parenthesis. The counterexample is a later occurrence in the same notebook, not a conjectural interpretation. The earlier 1971-270.7 had already distinguished the characteristic-zero commutativity statement.
fate: Already distinguished in \citet[Theorem I; \S III, Remark (3.14a)]{lazard1955formal}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: the literal assertion is refuted; the corrected versions are established.

title: Strict coordinate changes versus classification of laws
notes: The change \(z=\varphi(x)=x+a_1x^2+\cdots\) defines isomorphism. The speaker expressly says that classifying laws is different from classifying their isomorphism classes.
statement: A strict isomorphism \(F\to G\) is \(\varphi\in xA[[x]]\) with \(\varphi'(0)=1\) and \(\varphi(F(x,y))=G(\varphi(x),\varphi(y))\). A general isomorphism instead allows \(\varphi'(0)\in A^\times\). The functor of laws and its quotient by coordinate changes are different classification problems.
reconstruction: The adjective ``strict'' is supplied. The inverse expansion should be \(\varphi^{-1}(z)=z-a_1z^2+\cdots\); the notebook mixes the argument \(x\) with the output variable \(z\).
fate: Classical coordinate-change action: \citet[\S I, (1.4)--(1.8)]{lazard1955formal}; earlier occurrence 1971-270.5 distinguishes full and strict changes.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: standard, with the law/moduli distinction preserved.

title: Logarithm of a formal law
notes: A series \(g(x)=x+\cdots\) is called a logarithm when \(F(x,y)=g^{-1}(g(x)+g(y))\).
statement: A normalized logarithm is a strict homomorphism \(g:F\to\widehat{\mathbb G}_a\): \(g(F(x,y))=g(x)+g(y)\), \(g(0)=0\), \(g'(0)=1\). Its formal inverse exists because its linear coefficient is a unit.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: standard; integral or positive-characteristic existence is not automatic.

title: Canonical invariant differential
notes: For the shift \(x\mapsto F(x,t)\), invariance is \(\psi(F(x,t))\partial_xF(x,t)=\psi(x)\). The canonical differential is \(\omega_F=dx/\partial_yF(x,0)\).
statement: For a commutative one-dimensional formal law over a commutative ring \(A\), put \(b(x)=\partial_yF(x,y)|_{y=0}\), so \(b(0)=1\). Then \(\omega_F=b(x)^{-1}dx\) is translation invariant. Every invariant differential is \(c\omega_F\), \(c\in A\); thus normalization at the identity gives uniqueness.
reconstruction: The inverse is the formal inverse of the unit series \(b\); the parameter is held fixed during differentiation. No analytic differential form or integration is assumed.
fate: Pre-lecture invariant-differential construction: \citet[\S1]{honda1968formal}; earlier occurrences 1971-268.12 and 1971-270.8 cover invariant differentials and the logarithm.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established over arbitrary coefficient rings for commutative laws.

title: Existence and uniqueness of the normalized rational logarithm
notes: The ``Lazard lemma'' says that if \(A\) is a \(\mathbb Q\)-module, every formal group has a logarithm. The proof integrates \(\omega_F\), then evaluates at \(x=0\) to identify the integration constant.
statement: If \(A\) is a commutative unital \(\mathbb Q\)-algebra, then \(g(x)=\int_0^x b(t)^{-1}\,dt\) is the unique normalized logarithm of a commutative one-dimensional formal law. Hence any two such laws over \(A\) are uniquely strictly isomorphic by the composite of their logarithms and inverse logarithms.
reconstruction: ``\(\mathbb Q\)-module'' is interpreted as a compatible \(\mathbb Q\)-algebra structure on the given ring. The printed pointer ``Mat. 13:6'' resolves to Honda, not to a Russian publication of Lazard.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: proved; denominators explain the restriction on the base.

title: The universal rational law
notes: With \(g(x)=x+\sum_{i\ge1}g_ix^{i+1}\), the ring \(\mathbb Q[g_1,g_2,\ldots]\) carries a universal law, and every law is obtained by a coefficient homomorphism.
statement: The functor sending a commutative \(\mathbb Q\)-algebra \(A\) to its commutative one-dimensional formal laws is represented by \(\mathbb Q[g_1,g_2,\ldots]\), using \(F=g^{-1}(g(x)+g(y))\). The specialization sends \(g_i\) to the normalized logarithm coefficients. This represents laws in a chosen coordinate, not isomorphism classes.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established and consistent with rationalization of the Lazard ring.

title: Presentation of the integral universal coefficient ring
notes: The notes form \(\Lambda=\mathbb Z[a_{ij}]/J\), where \(J\) is generated by associativity coefficients and \(a_{ij}-a_{ji}\), with \(\deg a_{ij}=i+j-1\).
statement: Let \(i,j\ge1\), put \(F=x+y+\sum a_{ij}x^iy^j\), and quotient the polynomial ring by all coefficients of its associator and by all symmetry relations. For every commutative unital \(A\), ring maps \(\Lambda\to A\) correspond bijectively to commutative one-dimensional formal laws over \(A\).
reconstruction: The positive indices exclude pure higher powers and incorporate the identity laws. The grading uses half the usual topological degree.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established; representability does not itself prove polynomiality.

title: Lazard polynomiality and rationalization
notes: \(\Lambda=\mathbb Z[a_i]\), one generator of every degree \(i\ge1\), and \(\Lambda\otimes\mathbb Q=\mathbb Q[g_i]\).
statement: The coefficient ring of the universal commutative one-dimensional formal law is noncanonically a graded polynomial ring \(\mathbb Z[t_1,t_2,\ldots]\), \(\deg t_i=i\). Under rationalization logarithm coefficients give polynomial coordinates. A choice of integral generators is not canonical.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established; previous occurrence 1971-268.11 concerns the same universal-ring theorem.

title: Indecomposables linearize associativity
notes: The quotient by decomposables makes products of positive-degree coefficients zero and turns the associator into a linear equation for \(h=F-x-y\). A marginal gloss wrongly describes decomposables using arbitrary nonunits.
statement: For the augmented graded ring \(\Lambda\), use \(I=\bigoplus_{n>0}\Lambda_n\). Indecomposables are \(I/I^2\), or the augmented ring \(\Lambda/I^2\) if degree zero is retained. Modulo \(I^2\), associativity is \(h(x,y)+h(x+y,z)=h(y,z)+h(x,y+z)\). Products of positive-degree elements, not products of arbitrary nonunits, generate \(I^2\).
reconstruction: The margin is repaired using the unambiguous main-text phrase ``products of two of nonzero degree''. Taking nonunits literally would include integers such as \(2\) and alter degree zero.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: valid after the augmentation-ideal correction.

title: Classify homogeneous additive two-cocycles
notes: \ru{Задача: найти все решения} of \(h(x,y)+h(x+y,z)=h(y,z)+h(x,y+z)\), homogeneous polynomials over a ring \(K\). The surrounding formal-group problem requires symmetry; the page also temporarily studies nonsymmetric cycles.
statement: For each \(n\ge2\), classify normalized homogeneous \(h\in K[x,y]\) of degree \(n\) satisfying the displayed cocycle equation, and distinguish the symmetric submodule. In the symmetric case every solution is uniquely \(aC_n\), where \(C_n=((x+y)^n-x^n-y^n)/d_n\), \(d_n=p\) if \(n\) is a power of a prime \(p\), and \(d_n=1\) otherwise. This formula holds over every commutative ring via integral coefficients.
reconstruction: The exact symmetric answer is supplied from literature; the notebook states the task and develops its cohomological calculation over subsequent meetings. Nonsymmetric cycles must not be discarded before the distinction is made.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: the symmetric problem was already solved; the lecture is an exposition, not an orphan open question.

title: Primitive polynomial Hopf algebra and comodules
notes: \(K[x]\) has \(\Delta x=x\otimes1+1\otimes x\); a comodule is described as \(N\to A\otimes N\), and \(K\) is the trivial comodule.
statement: For the graded coalgebra \(C=K[x]\) with primitive generator, a left comodule is a \(K\)-module \(N\) with coaction \(\rho:N\to C\otimes_KN\) satisfying coassociativity and the counit identity. The trivial coaction on \(K\) is \(1\mapsto1\otimes1\). Internal polynomial degree and cohomological degree produce the two gradings.
reconstruction: The base-module structure and both coaction axioms are made explicit. ``Abelian group'' alone is insufficient for a general coefficient ring.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: standard with the specified category.

title: The two-cocycle exact sequence requires coalgebra cohomology
notes: The page writes \(0\to\{c((x+y)^n-x^n-y^n)\}\to L\to\operatorname{Ext}^{2,n}_{K[x]}(K,K)\to0\).
statement: For the normalized cobar complex of the primitive coalgebra \(K[x]\), \(Z^{2,n}=\{h:\delta h=0\}\), \(B^{2,n}=\{c((x+y)^n-x^n-y^n):c\in K\}\), and \(0\to B^{2,n}\to Z^{2,n}\to H^{2,n}\to0\). This is comodule cohomology (or dual divided-power algebra cohomology under suitable graded duality), not ordinary module Ext over the polynomial algebra.
reconstruction: The category is an essential emendation. Over a field, ordinary \(\operatorname{Ext}_{K[x]}^2(K,K)=0\), while the cobar group in characteristic \(p\) need not vanish. The leftmost term is the image subgroup, not an injective copy of every scalar \(c\).
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: correct as a cobar exact sequence; the unqualified Ext notation is misleading.

title: Quadratic and cubic cocycles: a mistaken characteristic
notes: For degree 2 the notes give \(cxy\). For degree 3 they give \(C_1x^2y+C_2xy^2\), write \(\widetilde\Lambda=\mathbb Z+\mathbb Z_3\), and claim \(x^2y\) is a cocycle over \(\mathbb Z_3\)-modules.
statement: Degree2 normalized cocycles are \(cxy\). In degree 3, direct expansion gives \(\delta(C_1x^2y+C_2xy^2)=2(C_1-C_2)xyz\), with \(\delta h=h(x,y)+h(x+y,z)-h(y,z)-h(x,y+z)\). Thus \(x^2y\) is a cocycle when \(2=0\), not when \(3=0\). The universal coefficient module without symmetry is \(\mathbb Z^2/\langle2(e_1-e_2)\rangle\simeq\mathbb Z\oplus\mathbb Z/2\); imposing symmetry leaves \(\mathbb Z\).
reconstruction: \oursComputed\ The polynomial expansion and independent evaluations in characteristics 2 and3 were both checked in the included formal-check script. The two visible subscripts3 in the scan are faithful notebook errors, not transcription corrections.
fate: Corrected symmetric case agrees with \citet[\S~II, Lemma~3]{lazard1955formal}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: the literal characteristic 3 claim is disproved by the displayed defect.

title: Minimal resolutions simplify the cohomology differential
notes: ``Choose the resolution correctly: all cycles without boundaries (minimal resolution).''
statement: For a connected graded algebra \(A\) over a field \(k\), a minimal graded free resolution of the augmentation module has differential with entries in \(A_{>0}\). Applying \(\operatorname{Hom}_A(-,k)\) makes that differential zero. Such a minimality argument does not hold unchanged over every coefficient ring.
reconstruction: The field and connected-grading hypotheses specify a valid version of the terse method; the notes have not established minimality over arbitrary \(K\).
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: standard under the stated hypotheses.

title: Divided-power multiplication on the dual
notes: \(K_*[x]=\operatorname{Hom}_K(K[x],K)\), \((x_*^n,x^m)=\delta_{nm}\), and \(x_*^nx_*^m=\binom{n+m}{n}x_*^{n+m}\).
statement: The graded dual of the primitive polynomial coalgebra has basis \(X_n\) and multiplication \(X_nX_m=\binom{n+m}{n}X_{n+m}\). This is the divided-power algebra. The full dual is its degree completion; the distinction matters when forming tensor products and duals.
reconstruction: The completion convention is supplied because the notebook initially uses full Hom, later continuous duality (P476).
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established; the displayed multiplication is independently determined by the binomial coproduct.

title: Characteristic-p factorization of the divided-power algebra
notes: The dual is written as \(\prod B_q\), with \(B_q=\mathbb Z_p[y_{p^i}]/(y_{p^i}^{p})\), and the text says it is enough to consider \(\mathbb Z_p\) and \(\mathbb Q\).
statement: Over \(k=\mathbb F_p\), the graded divided-power algebra is \(\bigotimes_{i\ge0}k[Y_i]/(Y_i^p)\), \(\deg Y_i=p^i\); its full dual version is the degree-completed tensor product. Over \(\mathbb Q\) it is isomorphic to a polynomial algebra by \(X_n\mapsto t^n/n!\). Passage from field calculations to an integral conclusion requires the finite-generation and torsion argument in each degree.
reconstruction: \(\mathbb Z_p\) here denotes the field with \(p\) elements, not the p-adic integers. An ordinary direct product of algebras would introduce unrelated idempotents and is not the asserted factorization.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: valid after distinguishing tensor product, completion, and coefficient fields.

title: Lazard theorem restated through indecomposables
notes: \(\Lambda=\mathbb Z[a_1,a_2,\ldots]\), \(\deg a_n=n\ge1\); the proposed proof passes to \(\bar\Lambda=\Lambda/(\text{decomposables})\).
statement: The universal commutative formal-law ring is polynomial; its positive indecomposables form one free rank-one group in every positive degree. Linearized relations describe those indecomposables, but a generation and torsion argument is still needed to recover the polynomial ring.
reconstruction: The phrase ``universal ring for polynomials'' is read degree by degree as a representing coefficient module with square-zero multiplication in positive degree.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established; no separate publication or new result is implied by this repeat.

title: An equivalent symmetric cocycle identity
statement: For a symmetric normalized polynomial \(h\), the identity displayed in the notes is equivalent to \(h(x,y)+h(x+y,z)=h(y,z)+h(x,y+z)\). To recover the latter, interchange \(x\) and \(z\) in the former and use symmetry.
reconstruction: The equation is not a mistranscription of the usual cocycle identity; it is equivalent in the explicitly stated symmetric context.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: correct with the symmetry hypothesis retained.

title: Resolution of the primitive coalgebra
notes: The sequence \(A[x]\to A[x]\otimes\bar A[y]\to A[x]\otimes\bar A[y]\otimes\bar A[z]\to\cdots\) is called a bar resolution; \(\bar A[y]\) has zero constant term.
statement: For the coaugmented coalgebra \(C=A[x]\), use the normalized cofree comodule resolution, whose reduced factors are \(\bar C=\ker\varepsilon\). The associated cobar cochain groups are \(A\), \(\bar C\), \(\bar C^{\otimes2}\), and so on; the differential inserts the reduced coproduct with alternating signs.
reconstruction: ``Cobar'' and ``comodule'' specify the variance omitted by the notebook. The polynomial coalgebra is free as an \(A\)-module, so the relative normalized construction has the needed underlying-module exactness.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: standard once the category is fixed.

title: Ordinary module Hom cannot substitute for comodule Hom
notes: The notes label the functor \(\operatorname{Hom}_{A[x]}(\mathcal A,A)\), call the resolution terms \(A[x]\)-modules, and obtain polynomial cochains.
statement: The intended polynomial cochains arise from \(\operatorname{Hom}_{C\text{-comod}}(A,-)\), or from continuous Hom over the dual divided-power algebra. They do not arise from the displayed ordinary polynomial-module Ext computation. For a field \(k\), the two-term free resolution \(0\to k[x]\xrightarrow{x}k[x]\to k\to0\) proves \(\operatorname{Ext}^2_{k[x]}(k,k)=0\).
reconstruction: \ours\ The displayed two-term free resolution independently proves the vanishing of ordinary module Ext in degree two. This is a mathematical notation repair confirmed by the explicit dual algebra introduced on P476. It does not assert that the speaker intended the incorrect ordinary-module calculation.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: the category omission must remain visible in any faithful edition.

title: Normalized coboundaries and the four-term differential
notes: The boundary of \(x^n\) is \((x+y)^n-x^n-y^n\). A later shorthand writes only two terms for the differential of \(h\), and notes that reduction removes constant terms.
statement: The normalized cobar differential is \(d f(x,y)=f(x+y)-f(x)-f(y)\), and \(d h(x,y,z)=h(x+y,z)-h(y,z)-h(x,y+z)+h(x,y)\). Thus degree-two cycles are precisely additive cocycles. The two displayed substitution terms require their reduced-coproduct corrections.
reconstruction: The four-term formula is supplied explicitly to disambiguate the abbreviated P467 formula; P476 later records all four terms correctly.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established; the normalized and unreduced versions should not be mixed.

title: Graded algebra cohomology
notes: For \(A=\bigoplus_{n\ge0}A_n\), the notes augment to \(A_0\), choose a graded free resolution \(C_\bullet\to A_0\), and put \(H^s(A)=\ker d_{s+1}^*/\operatorname{im}d_s^*\).
statement: For a nonnegatively graded augmented algebra over \(A_0\), define \(\operatorname{Ext}_A^{s,t}(A_0,A_0)\) using a graded projective or free resolution; \(s\) is resolution degree and \(t\) records internal degree. The augmentation is projection to degree zero, and \(A_0\) is made an \(A\)-module through it.
fate: Classical derived-functor definition; the notebook cites \citet{cartaneilenberg1956homological,maclane1963homology}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: standard; this is algebra-module Ext, as appropriate after dualizing the earlier coalgebra.

title: Existence of resolutions and independence of the answer
notes: The two stated assertions are that a free resolution exists and that \(H^s(A)\) is independent of the chosen resolution.
statement: Every graded module over a graded ring has a graded free resolution. Comparison maps lifting the identity are unique up to chain homotopy; applying graded \(\operatorname{Hom}\) therefore yields canonically isomorphic Ext groups for any two projective resolutions.
reconstruction: This general theorem does not automatically make the particular relative bar resolution free: its terms also require freeness of the reduced algebra over the base, or a suitable projective/relative version.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: proved well before the lecture.

title: Yoneda multiplication by lifting cocycles
notes: A representative \(C_i\to A_0\) is lifted to maps between the resolutions, and composition with a representative \(C_j\to A_0\) yields \(C_{i+j}\to A_0\).
statement: Lift a cocycle of cohomological degree \(i\) to a degree-\(i\) chain map of the resolution, then compose with a degree-\(j\) cocycle. The resulting degree-\(i+j\) class is independent of lifts and representatives and defines the associative Yoneda product, with the order fixed by this composition convention.
reconstruction: The dashed arrows in the scan are chain-map lifts, not canonical maps on the individual free modules. The diagram's existence uses projectivity and exactness.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: standard.

title: Ext need not be graded commutative
notes: \(H(A)\) is said to be noncommutative ``in a genuine sense'', even though the starting algebra is commutative; a parenthesis contrasts Hopf-algebra examples in topology.
statement: The Yoneda algebra of the augmentation module of a commutative algebra need not obey the graded commutativity rule. For example, if \(A=k\oplus V\) with \(V^2=0\), \(2\le\dim_kV<\infty\), then its normalized bar-cochain differential vanishes and \(\operatorname{Ext}_A(k,k)\cong T(V^*)\). Additional Hopf and symmetry structure is required for standard graded commutativity theorems.
reconstruction: \ours\ The square-zero example follows directly from the next bar differential: every product of two reduced elements vanishes, while concatenation remains free. It gives a precise counterexample; the claim that topology has only commutative rings is read as a comment on the examples under discussion, not as a universal assertion about topology.
fate: Buchstaber's later construction explicitly uses a noncommutative cohomology Hopf algebra: \citet[Introduction]{buchstaber1976twovaluedII}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: the algebraic warning is correct; the historical aside should not be promoted to a general theorem.

title: Homological classification of multivalued formal groups
notes: The single sentence says that classification of multivalued groups rests on the preceding noncommutative cohomology ring.
statement: The recoverable content is a method announcement: use bar-construction cohomology and its noncommutative product to impose associativity and extension conditions for multivalued formal laws. No number of values, complete axioms, coefficient hypotheses, or classification theorem is stated here.
reconstruction: The later two-valued theory supplies a documented continuation, not missing hypotheses to be retroactively inserted into the notebook. In the 1976 paper the ground ring excludes elements of order two; its first-type computation and second-type reduced-base theorem are more specific results than this sentence.
fate: The method is explicitly outlined in \citet[\S~IV, p.~174]{buchstaber1973classification}, received on 3 January 1973; the detailed realization appears in \citet[Introduction and \S1]{buchstaber1976twovaluedII}, received 28 April 1975. The exact all-multivalued classification cannot be claimed from these sources.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: the announced method has a published two-valued realization; the notebook does not formulate a larger open problem.

title: Normalized bar resolution and its signs
notes: With \(\bar A=\bigoplus_{n>0}A_n\), \(C_s=A\otimes_{A_0}\bar A^{\otimes s}\), and the differential merges adjacent entries. The corrected line says the sign exponent is the position when every element is even.
statement: Over a field, or when the reduced pieces are suitably projective over the base, the augmented normalized bar resolution computes Ext. In the all-even internal-degree case, \(d(a_0[a_1|\cdots|a_s])=a_0a_1[a_2|\cdots|a_s]+\sum_{j=1}^{s-1}(-1)^ja_0[a_1|\cdots|a_ja_{j+1}|\cdots|a_s]\). In a suspended graded convention the remaining signs obey the Koszul rule.
reconstruction: The notebook itself repairs the sign qualification. Exactness is supplied by the usual bar contraction; freeness over \(A\) requires the stated base-module hypothesis.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: standard under the specified projectivity and sign convention.

title: Dual bar differential and its correct target
notes: The notes identify \(\operatorname{Hom}_A(C_s,A_0)\) with \((\bar A^*)^{\otimes s}\), insert reduced coproducts, and then write \(\operatorname{im}\bar\Delta\subset\overline{A^*}\).
statement: Under degreewise finite projectivity and graded duality, multiplication dualizes to \(\Delta:A^*\to A^*\widehat\otimes A^*\), and on the augmentation ideal \(\bar\Delta\alpha=\Delta\alpha-\alpha\otimes1-1\otimes\alpha\) takes values in \(\bar A^*\widehat\otimes\bar A^*\). The dual bar differential inserts this reduced coproduct with the bar signs. Without these finiteness conventions one must retain \(\operatorname{Hom}_{A_0}(\bar A^{\otimes s},A_0)\), rather than identify it with a tensor product of duals.
reconstruction: The tensor square missing in the target is visible as an error in both transcription and scan; the preceding diagram already has \(A^*\otimes A^*\). Completion or graded finite pieces resolve the infinite-dimensional duality.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: correct after the duality hypotheses and target correction.

title: Concatenation represents the Yoneda product
notes: The product of \([\alpha_1|\cdots|\alpha_s]\) and \([\alpha'_1|\cdots|\alpha'_{s'}]\) is the concatenated word.
statement: On the tensor cobar model, concatenate words. The differential is a derivation for this multiplication with respect to cohomological degree; hence it descends to cohomology and agrees with the Yoneda multiplication, subject to the choice of ordering convention in 1972-282.3.
reconstruction: In general concatenation is not commutative on cochains or on cohomology. This observation explains the method announced immediately above, without supplying its later classification theorem.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: standard.

title: Completed divided powers and continuous duality
notes: \(A\) is additively \(\Lambda[[X]]\), with \(X_nX_m=\binom{n+m}{n}X_{n+m}\). Its compact dual consists of functionals nonzero on only finitely many basis elements. The next page uses a hatted tensor-product symbol.
statement: Use the degree-completed divided-power algebra and its continuous dual over discrete \(\Lambda\). The dual is \(\Lambda[x]\), paired by \(\langle x^n,X_m\rangle=\delta_{nm}\). In characteristic \(p\), the completion is \(\widehat{\bigotimes}_{i\ge0}\Lambda[Y_i]/(Y_i^p)\) when \(\Lambda\) is an \(\mathbb F_p\)-algebra. Finite internal-degree computations may instead use the graded algebra.
reconstruction: This completion convention clarifies the ordinary product sign on P463. ``Compact'' is the notebook's term for finite-support continuous functionals; it does not mean an arbitrary algebraic dual.
fate: Standard duality used in the later method; \citet[Introduction]{buchstaber1976twovaluedII}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established, with the topology specified.

title: The binomial coproduct
notes: Pairing multiplication with \(x_n\) gives coefficients \(\binom ni\), and the notes set \(x_n=x^n\), obtaining \(\Delta x^n=(x\otimes1+1\otimes x)^n\).
statement: For the preceding duality, \(\langle\Delta x^n,X_i\otimes X_j\rangle=\binom{i+j}{i}\delta_{n,i+j}\); therefore \(\Delta x^n=\sum_{i=0}^n\binom ni x^i\otimes x^{n-i}\). Its reduced coproduct omits the two endpoint terms.
reconstruction: The stray star on one \(x_j\) in the first expression is a notation slip: all factors belong to the same dual polynomial coalgebra. The subsequent complete formula removes the ambiguity.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: correct, with one local notation correction.

title: Cobar cycles and boundaries recover the Lazard equation
notes: Expanding the two reduced coproducts produces six terms, cancels the two \(h(x,z)\) terms, and gives the boxed four-term Lazard relation and a short exact sequence.
statement: In internal degree \(n\), \(Z^{2,n}=\ker d_3^*\) consists of normalized homogeneous additive two-cocycles, \(B^{2,n}=\operatorname{im}d_2^*\) consists of \(c((x+y)^n-x^n-y^n)\), and \(0\to B^{2,n}\to Z^{2,n}\to\operatorname{Ext}_A^{2,n}(\Lambda,\Lambda)\to0\) holds in the graded or continuous divided-power category.
reconstruction: Unlike the ambiguous polynomial-module notation on P467, \(A\) now has the correct divided-power multiplication. The single \(d_3\) without a star in the expansion is a notation slip, since the domain and the adjacent formulas are cochains.
fate: Same cocycle calculation as \citet[\S~II, Lemma~3]{lazard1955formal}; the later homological approach is documented in \citet[Introduction]{buchstaber1976twovaluedII}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established; the symmetric restriction remains a further step.

title: Recovering the integral calculation from fields
notes: Because the equation does not involve \(\Lambda\), the notes say it suffices to consider \(\mathbb F_p\)-modules and \(\mathbb Q\).
statement: In any fixed degree the integral coefficient-and-relation module is finitely generated. Its rational rank and its dimensions modulo every prime determine whether it is free of a specified rank, via the structure theorem for finitely generated abelian groups. Base change of kernels or Ext is not automatic; the argument should be made on the finite relation presentation or with the appropriate universal-coefficient sequence.
reconstruction: This supplies the missing integral bridge. Merely observing that an equation has integral coefficients does not justify identifying its solutions over an arbitrary ring with a base change of a field solution space.
fate: Lazard's integral coefficient argument provides the target conclusion: \citet[\S~II, Lemma~3 and Theorem II]{lazard1955formal}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: a valid proof strategy with the finite-presentation and torsion step supplied.

title: Ext of a truncated polynomial factor: the characteristic-two exception
notes: For every prime \(p\), the notes write \(H^*(A_i)=\Lambda_p(u_i)\otimes\mathbb F_p[v_i]\), \(|u_i|=(1,p^i)\), \(|v_i|=(2,p^{i+1})\), and list degree-two generators \(u_iu_j\) for \(i<j\) and \(v_k\).
statement: For \(A_i=k[t]/(t^p)\), \(k=\mathbb F_p\), \(|t|=p^i\), odd \(p\) gives \(\operatorname{Ext}_{A_i}(k,k)=\Lambda(u_i)\otimes k[v_i]\) in the displayed bidegrees. At \(p=2\) it is instead \(k[u_i]\), with \(v_i=u_i^2\), not an independent polynomial generator. Thus the listed vector-space basis in cohomological degree two can still be used if this identification is stated.
reconstruction: \ours\ For \(p=2\), the reduced augmentation ideal has square zero, so its one-generator tensor bar cochain algebra has zero differential; all powers of the degree-one class survive. This directly disproves the exterior factor. The odd-prime periodic resolution alternates multiplication by \(t\) and \(t^{p-1}\).
fate: The normalized bar construction supplies the correction; \citet[Ch.X]{cartaneilenberg1956homological}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: the uniformly stated ring formula is false at two; the corrected ring calculation is standard.

title: An associative noncommutative one-dimensional formal group
notes: The emphatic example is \(F=x+y+axy^p\) over \(\mathbb F_p[a]/(a^2)\), and the text says one-dimensional noncommutative groups exist with torsion.
statement: For any prime \(p\), this series is a formal group law. Its associator is zero because \((y+z)^p=y^p+z^p\) and \(a^2=0\); its commutator is \(a(xy^p-yx^p)\ne0\). Therefore commutativity fails over this nonreduced torsion base.
reconstruction: \oursComputed\ The included script checks the associator symbolically modulo \((p,a^2)\) and independently by arithmetic in dual-number rings for \(p=2,3,5\). The general proof is the Frobenius identity just given. This is the speaker's own later correction to 1972-276.2, not an invented counterexample.
fate: The characteristic-two version was already given by \citet[\S~I, after Theorem I]{lazard1955formal}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: correct; it requires nilpotents as well as torsion, so torsion alone is not asserted to force noncommutativity.

title: Cocycles and actual laws: the square-zero qualification
notes: After the example, the notes say ``There are as many of them as there are cycles.''
statement: If \(I\) is an ideal with \(I^2=0\), normalized \(I\)-valued additive two-cocycles correspond exactly to laws \(F=x+y+h\) whose nonlinear coefficients lie in \(I\): higher nonlinear compositions vanish. For unrestricted coefficients a first-order cocycle is only a candidate deformation; higher associativity obstructions must be solved. Modding out by coordinate changes also identifies cocycles differing by a coboundary.
reconstruction: The local square-zero context makes the sentence valid. Extending it to arbitrary full laws or to their isomorphism classes would be false. Lazard gives noncommutative truncated laws over a reduced field that cannot extend to full one-dimensional laws.
fate: The extension distinction is explicit in \citet[\S~II, Theorem III and the following remark]{lazard1955formal}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: valid as an infinitesimal statement, not an unrestricted counting theorem.

title: Normalized binomial cocycles and one indecomposable per degree
notes: The \(v_k\) classes are linked to symmetric groups. The coefficients of \((x+y)^{p^{k+1}}-x^{p^{k+1}}-y^{p^{k+1}}\) are divisible by \(p\), and the bracketed formula divides by \(p\). The last mathematical line says there is one generator in every dimension.
statement: Write \(B_n=(x+y)^n-x^n-y^n\). Its coefficient gcd is \(d_n=p\) when \(n=p^r\), otherwise \(d_n=1\). The integral primitive polynomial \(C_n=B_n/d_n\) generates all symmetric normalized degree-\(n\) additive cocycles over any base. In the Lazard grading this yields one free indecomposable in degree \(n-1\), and the full polynomial-ring theorem follows with the generation argument.
reconstruction: The \(1/p\) normalization is actually present in the scan and in the transcription's diagram; it must not be reported as an omission. Over \(\mathbb F_p\), the unnormalized \(B_{p^r}\) is zero, whereas the reduction of the integral quotient need not be zero.
fate: Exact published theorem: \citet[\S~II, Lemma~3 and Theorem II]{lazard1955formal}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established since 1955; the semester closes an exposition of this result.

title: Homotopy smoothings and their equivalence
notes: A smoothing is a smooth \(N^n\) with a homotopy equivalence \(f:N\to M\); two are equivalent when a diffeomorphism of source manifolds makes the triangle commute up to homotopy.
statement: The object is the marked smooth homotopy structure set \(\mathcal S^{\mathrm{Diff}}(M)\): pairs \((N,f)\) modulo a diffeomorphism \(h:N_1\to N_2\) with \(f_2h\simeq f_1\). For an oriented target the marking determines the orientation of the source. This differs from a smoothing of a fixed topological manifold, where the comparison map is a homeomorphism.
reconstruction: The later notation \(hS\) on P481 and P488 makes the distinction explicit. For the surgery statements below we use closed connected manifolds of dimension at least six and fix a reference smooth or PL structure as appropriate.
fate: Definition and equivalence agree with \citet[pp.81--82]{sullivan1996triangulating}, notes circulated 1967.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: standard; the earlier letter S is retained as historical notation.

title: Twenty-eight smooth homotopy seven-spheres
notes: The page attributes \(\operatorname{card}S'(S^7)=28\) to Milnor. The prime after S is visually present but not defined.
statement: The group \(\Theta_7\) of oriented smooth homotopy seven-spheres up to oriented diffeomorphism is cyclic of order 28. The corresponding marked structure set over \(S^7\) has28 elements. This is not an assertion that there are28 unoriented diffeomorphism classes after forgetting the marking and orientation.
reconstruction: The interpretation of the unexplained prime is supplied by the precise established theorem. The counting theorem is due to Kervaire and Milnor, rather than a new seminar computation.
fate: \citet{kervairemilnor1963spheres}; the statement \(\Theta_7=\mathbb Z/28\) is also explicit in \citet[\S13.3]{ranicki2002surgery}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established since 1963.

title: Describe the homotopy structure set
notes: ``Description of \(S(M^n)\)—?'' The next paragraph says Sullivan solved the analogous PL formulation.
statement: For a fixed closed simply connected smooth \(n\)-manifold \(M\), \(n\ge6\), describe the marked homotopy structure set. Surgery gives \([\Sigma M_+,G/O]\to L_{n+1}(\mathbb Z)\curvearrowright\mathcal S^{\mathrm{Diff}}(M)\to[M,G/O]\to L_n(\mathbb Z)\), with exactness in pointed sets and an action on fibres. An individual numerical classification additionally requires computing the normal-invariant set and the obstruction and action maps.
reconstruction: The high-dimensional closed simply connected scope is an editorial reconstruction justified by the continuation on P488. It is not a universal solution in every dimension or fundamental group. This occurrence continues the normal-data and surgery themes of 1968-171.10, 1968-171.15, and 1968-173.2; the older homotopy-torus problem is narrower and receives no reused problem ID here.
fate: The structural answer predates the lecture: \citet[Theorem~3]{sullivan1996triangulating}; modern precise action form in \citet[Theorem~13.2]{ranicki2002surgery}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: the specified structural classification is established; the notebook asks no concrete uncomputed manifold case.

title: PL homotopy structures and the standard sphere
notes: Replacing diffeomorphisms by PL homeomorphisms gives \(PL(M)\), and \(PL(S^n)=\{S^n\}\) is asserted for \(n\ge5\).
statement: For a fixed PL manifold, define \(\mathcal S^{PL}(M)\) by PL source manifolds marked by homotopy equivalences, modulo PL homeomorphisms over the target up to homotopy. A PL homotopy sphere of dimension \(n\ge5\) is PL homeomorphic to the standard sphere, so this marked structure set is a singleton.
reconstruction: The statement concerns combinatorial PL manifold structures. It is not a uniqueness assertion for arbitrary singular triangulations, nor a smooth Poincare theorem.
fate: Classical high-dimensional PL Poincare result used in \citet[pp.69--72,81--82]{sullivan1996triangulating}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established in the stated PL high-dimensional setting.

title: Thom quotient and the bottom fibre sphere
notes: \(T_\xi=D(\xi)/S(\xi)\), and a fibre over a chosen point gives \(i:S^m\to T_\xi\) for an \(m\)-plane bundle.
statement: For a real vector bundle \(\xi\) over a finite CW complex, its Thom space is the quotient of its disk bundle by its sphere bundle. The compactified fibre over a basepoint embeds as \(S^m\). Adding a trivial line suspends the Thom space, so stable bundle statements correspond to stable maps of these spaces.
reconstruction: A fibre orientation specifies the sign of the degree of a restriction. The stable rank is allowed to increase; this matters for the next criterion.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: standard.

title: Thom coreducibility characterizes J-triviality
notes: \(\xi\) is called J-trivial if a map \(\varphi:T_\xi\to S^m\) has \(\deg(\varphi i)=1\). Connectedness is used to dismiss dependence on the chosen point.
statement: For a stable vector bundle over a connected finite CW complex, \(J(\xi)=0\) exactly when, after sufficient stabilization, its Thom space admits a map to the bottom sphere restricting to degree one on a fibre. Equivalently its associated stable sphere fibration is fibre homotopy trivial. A degree-one restriction also forces orientability; connectedness alone does not make an unoriented sign choice canonical.
reconstruction: The stable qualification is already suggested by ``large dimension'' in the notes. The precise statement is stable coreducibility, not a claim that every unstable sphere bundle is linearly trivial.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established before the lecture.

title: Kernel of J versus a normal invariant
notes: \(K_J(M)\) is defined as stable bundles that are J-trivial. The later sequence treats it as the object represented by the smooth normal-invariant space.
statement: Bare stable bundle classes form \(\ker(\widetilde{KO}(M)\to J(M))\). The standard normal-invariant set instead records pairs \((\xi,\varphi)\), where \(\varphi\) is a specified stable spherical trivialization, modulo the corresponding equivalence. These pairs are classified by \([M,G/O]\), with \(G/O\) the homotopy fibre of \(BO\to BG\). Forgetting \(\varphi\) maps onto the kernel but can identify distinct normal invariants.
reconstruction: This is an essential refinement, not a change of notation alone. P488 draws a trivialization but its prose still suppresses it. The homotopy fibre represents a chosen null-homotopy; the set-theoretic kernel of maps into BO and BG does not by itself retain that data.
fate: The pair is explicit in \citet[p.80]{sullivan1996triangulating}; see also \citet[Proposition~9.21]{ranicki2002surgery}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: the normal-invariant interpretation is established; the literal bare-bundle functor is insufficient for the asserted classification.

title: Atiyah normal-bundle difference
notes: Atiyah's theorem, referenced as Matematika10:5, yields \(S(M)\to K_J(M)\), described only as a difference.
statement: If \(f:N\to M\) is a homotopy equivalence of closed smooth manifolds and \(g\) is a homotopy inverse, then \(\xi=g^*\nu_N+\tau_M\) has trivial stable spherical fibration. Equivalently \(J(\tau_N)=J(f^*\tau_M)\). The associated structure normal invariant further includes the trivialization induced by the homotopy equivalence.
reconstruction: The precise difference formula is supplied by the later P481 and P488 occurrences. The Matematika pointer resolves exactly to the1966 Russian translation of Atiyah's1961 paper; Buchstaber was its translator.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: an established homotopy-invariance theorem for the stable spherical normal data, not for the vector bundle itself.

title: The PL surgery classification and the periodic obstruction
notes: A crossed-out ``always'' is replaced by dimension congruences. The display injects \(PL(M)\) into \(K_{PLJ}(M)\) and lists cokernels \(\mathbb Z\) for \(n\equiv0\) and \(\mathbb Z/2\) for \(n\equiv2\pmod4\).
statement: For a closed simply connected PL manifold of dimension \(n\ge6\), the refined normal invariant gives an injection \(\mathcal S^{PL}(M)\to[M,G/PL]\), whose image is the zero fibre of the surgery obstruction \(\theta:[M,G/PL]\to L_n(\mathbb Z)\). Here \(L_n(\mathbb Z)=\mathbb Z\) for \(n\equiv0\), \(\mathbb Z/2\) for \(n\equiv2\), and zero for odd \(n\). Thus in odd dimensions the normal invariant is a bijection. The exactness is that of pointed sets; a group cokernel is not implied.
reconstruction: Compactness, absence of boundary, simple connectivity, stable trivialization data, and the dimension restriction are supplied. With boundary there are separate relative conventions; with nontrivial fundamental group the obstruction groups involve the group ring. A terminal group in an exact sequence is not automatically its cokernel.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: the qualified PL theorem is established; the notebook display is too compressed to support an unconditional group exact sequence.

title: Sullivan computation of the PL normal-invariant homotopy groups
notes: The notes say Sullivan computed the homotopy groups of the representing space for \(K_{PLJ}\), without writing the groups.
statement: For the refined classifying space \(G/PL\), the positive homotopy groups are abstractly \(\mathbb Z\) in degrees divisible by four, \(\mathbb Z/2\) in degrees congruent to two modulo four, and zero in odd degrees. In dimensions at least five these agree with the simply connected surgery groups through the surgery obstruction. The degree-four comparison has a special normalization and should not be inferred from that high-dimensional statement.
reconstruction: The group formula comes from the cited literature. It is not present on this notebook page, which gives only the attribution. Modern G/PL denotes the stable version of Sullivan's F/PL.
fate: \citet[pp.69--72,83--84]{sullivan1996triangulating}; the high-dimensional identification is also in \citet[Remark~13.25]{ranicki2002surgery}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established, including the need to distinguish the dimension-four comparison map.

title: Smooth normal invariants: a reconstructed all-degree computation programme
notes: Immediately after the PL calculation: ``For \(K_J(M^n)\) it has not been done. A sequence for \(S(M^n)\) exists too.''
statement: Under the intended refinement \(K_J\rightsquigarrow[M,G/O]\), the remaining program is to determine \(\pi_q(G/O)\) in all degrees. For \(q\ge2\), the fibration gives \(\pi_q(O)\xrightarrow{J}\pi_q^S\to\pi_q(G/O)\to\pi_{q-1}(O)\xrightarrow{J}\pi_{q-1}^S\). Finite-degree calculations therefore require stable stems, the J maps, and extension data.
reconstruction: The notes do not name G/O, specify a degree range, or formulate an explicit conjecture. The all-degree program is a cautious reconstruction of the comparison sentence; taken literally for the bare kernel functor, a representing-space problem is not specified. No new finite range is invented.
fate: The reduction and low-degree tables are established in \citet[\S9.2]{ranicki2002surgery}. Finite stable-stem progress continues, for example \citet[Theorem~1.1]{burklundisaksenxu2026synthetic} (preprint 2024, online 2025, volume 2026), computing particular 82nd and83rd 2-primary stems, not all \(\pi_q(G/O)\).
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: many finite ranges are known; no complete all-degree numerical determination was located in the primary literature checked through the status date. The reconstructed all-degree computation programme remains unfinished; no specific finite unresolved group is asserted.
worth: A specific bounded range or extension question could justify research. The notebook supplies neither; attempting a wholesale new stable-stem computation would not be a sound chapter-sized development. We retain the exact-sequence reduction as annotation and claim no new theorem.

title: Homotopy structures distinguished from actual structures
notes: \(hS(M^n)\) means homotopy smoothings and \(ht(M^n)\) homotopy triangulations; the latter is said to be describable.
statement: These are the marked smooth and PL structure sets defined by homotopy equivalences, with source isomorphisms over the target up to homotopy. Actual smoothings or PL structures on a fixed topological manifold use homeomorphic comparison maps and require a separate equivalence convention.
reconstruction: The letter h supplies the qualification omitted in the initial P478 label. The notebook does not define every equivalence relation for actual, rather than homotopy, structures here.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: standard notation with the distinction retained.

title: Hauptvermutung: homology index and dimensional hypotheses
notes: A homeomorphism of manifolds can be replaced by a PL homeomorphism when M is simply connected and has no2-torsion in \(H^3\). The scan clearly places3 above H.
statement: A verified pre-lecture version is: if \(h:L\to M\) is a homeomorphism of compact closed simply connected PL manifolds of dimension at least six and \(H_3(M;\mathbb Z)\) has no2-torsion, then h is homotopic to a PL homeomorphism. Equivalently the integral \(H^4(M;\mathbb Z)\) has no2-torsion. For manifolds with boundary the corresponding simple-connectivity assumptions on boundary components are needed.
reconstruction: Replace superscript \(H^3\) by subscript \(H_3\), or by \(H^4\). These are different groups; the correction follows from Sullivan's original theorem and the universal coefficient theorem. ``Replace'' means homotope the given map, not assert isotopy. The missing compactness and dimension hypotheses must also be supplied.
fate: \citet[Main Theorem]{sullivan1967hauptvermutung}; precise obstruction and corollary in \citet[Theorem H and Corollary~1, pp.93--94]{sullivan1996triangulating}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: the corrected high-dimensional homotopy Hauptvermutung statement is established; the \(H^3\) sentence is not the published theorem.

title: The normal difference is independent of a marked representative
notes: For \(f:N\to M\), with homotopy inverse g, the notes form \(\tau_M+g^*\nu_N\), where \(\nu_N=-\tau_N\) stably, and ask as an exercise that equivalent smoothings induce isomorphic bundles.
statement: The virtual rank-zero class is \(\xi_f=[\tau_M]-g^*[\tau_N]\in\widetilde{KO}(M)\). If \(f_2h\simeq f_1\) for a diffeomorphism \(h:N_1\to N_2\), then \(g_2\simeq hg_1\), \(h^*\tau_{N_2}\cong\tau_{N_1}\), and \(\xi_{f_2}=\xi_{f_1}\). Homotopy inverses are themselves unique up to homotopy, so the construction is well defined.
reconstruction: \ours\ This is the complete solution of the stated elementary exercise, using pullback homotopy invariance. It proves equality of stable bundle classes; it does not by itself identify the chosen spherical trivializations in a normal invariant.
fate: Compatible with \citet[Theorem~3.6]{atiyah1961thom} and the refined construction of \citet[pp.80--81]{sullivan1996triangulating}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: the exercise is resolved under the stated stable interpretation.

title: J-triviality and proper fibrewise equivalence
notes: The resulting \(\xi\) is declared J-trivial, drawn as a proper homotopy equivalence \(\xi\to M\times\mathbb R^N\) over the identity of M.
statement: Atiyah's theorem makes the stable sphere bundle of \(\xi_f\) fibre homotopy trivial. In sufficiently large rank it may be represented by a proper fibrewise homotopy equivalence of the associated Euclidean bundles; compactifying the fibres gives a degree-one equivalence of sphere bundles. The proper and fibrewise qualifications are part of the data.
reconstruction: Ordinary homotopy equivalence of the uncompactified total spaces would be too weak: every vector-bundle total space retracts onto its base. The notebook's diagram and the word proper prevent that misreading.
fate: \citet[Theorem~3.6]{atiyah1961thom}; the proper-equivalence formulation is explicit in \citet[p.80]{sullivan1996triangulating}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established after stabilization.

title: Equivalence of the two J-triviality criteria
notes: A second definition asks for \(T(\xi)\to S^N\) restricting to a homotopy equivalence on the fibre sphere; equivalence is called Dold's theorem and an exercise.
statement: For a stable bundle over a connected finite CW complex, proper fibrewise triviality and the degree-one Thom coreduction criterion are equivalent after stabilization. Dold's fibrewise equivalence criterion supplies the step from a fibrewise map inducing homotopy equivalences to a fibre homotopy equivalence; Atiyah's stable cofibration argument supplies the Thom-space step.
reconstruction: This separates two ingredients hidden in the attribution. The exact cited Dold result is1955, Corollary~2, identified in Atiyah's Proposition~2.8 proof; it is not the unrelated Dold--Thom infinite-symmetric-product theorem.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: proved before the lecture; not an unfinished research exercise.

title: Four structure notations
notes: The page lists \(S(M)\), \(hS(M)\), \(t(M)\), and \(ht(M)\), respectively smoothings, homotopy smoothings, triangulations, and homotopy triangulations.
statement: The h-prefixed objects are the marked structure sets of homotopy equivalences, in the smooth and PL categories. The unprefixed terms refer to actual structures compatible with the underlying topological manifold. No new equivalence definition for the unprefixed sets is supplied here; later arguments explicitly concern \(hS(M)\).
reconstruction: We do not equate concordance, isotopy, and abstract diffeomorphism classes of actual structures, since the notebook does not choose between those notions.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: standard for the h-prefixed objects; the unprefixed notation alone does not specify a classification problem.

title: The set Phi must retain a specified trivialization
notes: \(\Phi(M)\) is called the set, then group, of stable smooth J-trivial bundles. A proper equivalence \(\varphi:\xi\to M\times\mathbb R^N\) is drawn, with \(N=\dim\xi\).
statement: The surgery construction needs stable equivalence classes of pairs \((\xi,\varphi)\), not only bundles admitting some such \(\varphi\). This refined \(\Phi(M)\) is \([M,G/O]\), equivalently the normal-bordism set of degree-one smooth normal maps after fixing the reference manifold M.
reconstruction: The drawing contains the required trivialization but the prose does not explicitly include it in the equivalence relation. We retain this distinction, as in 1972-287.7. The rank N in this paragraph is unrelated to the source manifold denoted N below.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: standard after the essential pair-data refinement.

title: Normal difference and its zero normalization
notes: For a homotopy equivalence \(\alpha:N\to M\) with inverse g, the class is \(g^*\nu_N+\tau_M\). The parenthesis mistakenly calls \(\nu_N\) the normal bundle of M. For the identity, the sum is trivial; for a homotopy equivalence, Atiyah--Dold supplies J-triviality.
statement: \(\nu_N\) is the stable normal bundle of the source N. Modulo a trivial summand, \(g^*\nu_N+\tau_M\) represents \(\tau_M-g^*\tau_N\), is zero for the identity structure, and has trivial stable spherical fibration for any homotopy-equivalence marking. Its refinement with the induced trivialization is the normal invariant.
reconstruction: The wrong base M in the explanatory parenthesis is legible in the scan and both transcriptions. Correcting it to N is necessary for the pullback by g even to have the stated domain.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established; the local source/target slip is corrected.

title: The simply connected surgery obstruction sequence
notes: Assuming \(\pi_1(M)=0\), the notes display \(hS(M)\to\Phi(M)\to P_n\), with \(P_n=0,\mathbb Z,\mathbb Z/2\) according to the dimension modulo four.
statement: For a closed simply connected smooth n-manifold with \(n\ge6\), \(\mathcal S^{\mathrm{Diff}}(M)\xrightarrow\eta[M,G/O]\xrightarrow\theta L_n(\mathbb Z)\) is exact in the sense that \(\operatorname{im}\eta=\theta^{-1}(0)\). The group \(L_n(\mathbb Z)\) is zero in odd dimensions, \(\mathbb Z\) in dimension \(4k\), and \(\mathbb Z/2\) in dimension \(4k+2\). The smooth obstruction map need not be surjective or additive.
reconstruction: The missing dimensional/compactness assumptions and the normal-invariant interpretation are supplied. A vanishing obstruction means normal bordism to a homotopy equivalence, not that the particular transverse representative already is one.
fate: Pre-lecture surgery theory: \citet[Theorem~3]{sullivan1996triangulating}; precise modern statement \citet[Theorem~13.2]{ranicki2002surgery}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established in the specified range.

title: Adding the reference normal bundle and passing to Thom spaces
notes:
The proper trivialization is summed with \(
u_M\), inducing \(T(\xi+
u_M)	o T(N+
u_M)\).
statement:
For an actual rank-r representative \(\xi\) and its fibrewise trivialization, summing with \(
u_M\) yields a proper equivalence to \(\varepsilon^r\oplus
u_M\), hence a Thom homotopy equivalence \(\varphi_0:T(\xi\oplus
u_M)\simeq\Sigma^rT(
u_M)\). In the notebook's N+ notation, N means a trivial bundle of that rank.
reconstruction: A homotopy inverse \(\sigma\) may be chosen. To keep dimensions consistent in the next construction, one suspends the Pontryagin--Thom collapse by r; alternatively one works throughout with virtual rank-zero Thom spectra.
fate: \citet[\S2]{atiyah1961thom}; the resulting normal-invariant construction is explicit in \citet[Proposition~9.43]{ranicki2002surgery}.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: standard once rank and suspension conventions are stated.

title: Pontryagin--Thom collapse of the reference embedding
notes: For \(M^n\subset\mathbb R^L\), a normal tube gives \(\lambda:S^L\to T(\nu_M)\), transverse to the zero section with preimage M.
statement: Embed the closed smooth manifold M in Euclidean space and identify a tubular neighbourhood with the normal disk bundle. Collapsing the complement of its interior to the Thom basepoint gives \(\lambda\); near the zero section it is smooth and transverse, and \(\lambda^{-1}(M)=M\). Its stable homotopy class is independent of the auxiliary embedding and tube in the appropriate normal-invariant formulation.
reconstruction: The zero section is an embedding into the Thom space; it is the collapse map that is transverse to that section, repairing the syntactic ambiguity in the second notebook sentence. This repeats the construction of1968-171.13.
fate: \citet[Example~9.41 and Theorem~9.42]{ranicki2002surgery}; the underlying construction is classical Pontryagin--Thom theory.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established.

title: Transversality produces a degree-one normal map
notes: Compose the collapse with a homotopy inverse \(\sigma\), deform it transverse to M, and set \(M_1=(\widetilde{\sigma\lambda})^{-1}(M)\). The boxed identity identifies its normal bundle as a pullback of \(\xi+\nu_M\).
statement:
With the suspension convention of1972-293.5, make \(\sigma\circ\Sigma^r\lambda:S^{L+r}	o T(\xi\oplus
u_M)\) transverse to the zero section. Its inverse image is a closed smooth n-manifold \(M_1\), and the restricted map \(f:M_1	o M\) has degree one with stable normal identification \(
u_{M_1}\cong f^*(\xi\oplus
u_M)\). This is a degree-one normal map representing the given normal invariant.
reconstruction: The degree-one property follows from the chosen fibre degree and Thom class; it is not written explicitly in the notebook but is indispensable for surgery. The equality is a stable bundle identification, not equality of unrelated ambient normal ranks.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: an established construction, not a new existence theorem.

title: How uniquely is the transverse manifold determined?
notes: The page asks how uniquely \(M_1\) is determined; the next page says all such manifolds are related by Morse surgeries, attributing the statement to Milnor--Kervaire.
statement: A fixed normal invariant determines a normal-bordism class of degree-one normal maps. Different transverse approximations and compatible Thom homotopies give a normal bordism; a handle decomposition of that bordism gives a finite sequence of surgeries compatible with the normal data. It does not determine the diffeomorphism type of \(M_1\), and equality of bare stable bundle classes is weaker than equality of normal invariants.
reconstruction: The exact theorem matching the notes is the normal-map bordism theorem, followed by the surgery/handle decomposition of a bordism. No unique Kervaire--Milnor theorem locator matching this entire compressed attribution was found, so that attribution remains only partial. The underlying questions were already present in 1968-171.15 and1968-173.2--3.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: resolved at the level of normal bordism; finer structure-set ambiguity is the next item.

title: Can surgery produce a homotopy equivalence?
notes: ``Is there a manifold there homotopy equivalent to M?'' The group \(P_n\) is called the obstruction to surgery to such an equivalence, and exactness is asserted.
statement: For the simply connected closed degree-one normal map in the high-dimensional range, its normal-bordism class contains a homotopy equivalence exactly when its surgery obstruction vanishes in \(L_n(\mathbb Z)\). In dimension \(4k\), the obstruction is the signature defect divided by eight; in dimension \(4k+2\) it is the Arf invariant of the surgery kernel's quadratic form; in odd dimensions it vanishes.
reconstruction: The obstruction formulas are supplied from the literature to make \(P_n\) substantive. They apply to the normal-map problem and require preliminary surgeries below the middle dimension, not to an arbitrary continuous map or arbitrary manifold.
fate: \citet[Theorem~13.2 and Example~13.3]{ranicki2002surgery}, consolidating the pre-1973 Browder--Novikov--Sullivan--Wall theorem.
present_status: As of 9 November 2026: established; this is an exposition of the surgery criterion.

title: The missing left term and h-cobordisms among films
notes: The sequence begins with a question mark before \(hS(M)\). Two structures yield Thom maps \(\beta_1,\beta_2\); a homotopy F is called a film, and the final question asks whether h-cobordisms occur among these films.
statement: For \(n\ge6\), the missing ambiguity is the action of \(L_{n+1}(\mathbb Z)\) on the smooth structure set. Structures with the same normal invariant lie in one action orbit. A transverse Thom homotopy represents a normal bordism \(W\to M\times I\); it can be changed relative to its ends to an h-cobordism precisely when its relative surgery obstruction is zero. Different films can change that obstruction by the image of \([\Sigma M_+,G/O]\to L_{n+1}(\mathbb Z)\).
reconstruction: This is an action exact sequence, not an ordinary group kernel-cokernel sequence.
